message: Repo layout pushed for PULSE-12. data/ is gitignored in full - generated warehouses are large, they change every run, and a committed .duckdb is a merge conflict nobody can resolve.
[PULSE-12] Cloned clean and the quickstart worked, except DuckDB wants to download an extension on first run so it needs network. Added a README line rather than vendoring it.

Branch convention so the board stays readable: pulse/PULSE-12-short-slug. The key goes first so a branch list sorts into something you can scan. PR template is in .github with a checklist - ticket link, what changed, how it was verified.
Sprint 1 close. Merged: PULSE-12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19. No CI yet, which is the biggest gap and is PULSE-32 next sprint.

[PULSE-26] docker-compose with Postgres is up. From here I would like us both running against both engines locally. The gap we do not want is SQL that works in DuckDB, ships, and meets Postgres for the first time in the cloud.
[PULSE-26] Two divergences already - date_trunc argument order and a window frame default. Both documented in the DDL rather than branched on.
Sprint 2 close. Bronze loads all eight sources, run context is recording, revenue and AOV definitions signed off by finance. One bug found and fixed (PULSE-23) and it was a silent one.

PULSE-32: CI is at nine minutes forty, which is close enough to the ten minute target to be a problem soon. Most of it is the warehouse build. Caching the generated dataset between jobs when the seed has not changed would take a couple of minutes off.

PULSE-117 raised. Trigger: the moment there are two schedules with a dependency between them. Raising it at the point of deciding not to do it, so it is a ticket rather than a recurring conversation with no memory.
[PULSE-32] CI is live. Lint, tests and a full pipeline build on generated data, against both DuckDB and containerised Postgres, under ten minutes. Red build blocks merge.
[PULSE-32] First run caught a Postgres-only cast error, which is exactly what it is for.

[PULSE-108] First Terraform draft priced out at roughly GBP 600 a month for a dev environment nobody uses at night - provisioned SQL and premium Databricks. That is how a platform gets switched off by finance in month three.

[PULSE-108] Serverless Postgres with auto-pause, Container Apps scaled to zero, smallest Databricks cluster with aggressive auto-termination, lifecycle rules to cool storage after 30 days. Dev is now about GBP 31. The estimate is committed next to the Terraform so a change that increases it shows up in the diff.
PULSE-107 is up as four Terraform modules. Review them separately if it is easier - storage and registry are dull, streaming and warehouse are where the decisions are.
One thing on PULSE-107: the Postgres module has a public network access flag defaulting to true. I assume that is for the dev convenience, but it should not be the default anyone inherits.
Correct, and thank you - that was me testing connectivity and forgetting. Default is false in PULSE-107 now, with dev overriding it explicitly in its tfvars so the exception is visible.

[PULSE-109] ADR-006 on managed Postgres over Synapse is up. The part that makes it useful is the revisit trigger with real numbers on it - gold over roughly 500GB, or p95 dashboard latency past 3s. Without that the conversation reopens every quarter on vibes.

Draft of the deploy workflows for PULSE-113 is on a branch, not up for review yet. Plan on PR, apply on merge behind an environment gate. The rollback path is the part I want people to poke at once it is up.
